title: At least 169 killed in Colombia's largest earthquake in years
facts: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake in Colombia killed at least 169 people.
Colombia's geological service reported the earthquake struck at 07:34 local time (12:34 GMT) at a depth of 103km in Chocó province.
Colombia's Association of Capital Cities (Asocapitales) reported at least 900 people injured in the earthquake.
The earthquake's epicenter was located near the village of San José del Palmar in Chocó province.
Mayor León Fabio Marín Moncada reported no deaths or injuries in San José del Palmar despite road damage.
The earthquake caused 85 deaths in the city of Cali, located about 200km from the epicenter.
Sixty-six people died in the city of Pereira in Colombia's coffee-growing region.
At least five people died in the city of Manizales as a result of the earthquake.
Regional airports in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago, and Buenaventura sustained damage.
Tremors from the earthquake were felt across Colombia as well as in Venezuela, Ecuador, and Panama.
Twin earthquakes in northern Venezuela killed more than 6,300 people less than two months earlier.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a national disaster situation following the earthquake.
Abelardo de la Espriella assumed office as President of Colombia on Friday prior to the earthquake.
EU chief Ursula von der Leyen stated the EU's Copernicus satellite was deployed to assist Colombian rescue operations.
El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele offered personnel and equipment to support disaster response in Colombia.
